name: IKS Anguish
_comment: R3.36, Module R3 SSD book page 3. A D6 hull converted to carry prisoners, so it is entered
as the D6 with the penal differences applied rather than re-read box by box: the F5/F5J pair
already in this directory differ in exactly two things, and the D6J's sheet shows the same
two. The ship data table gives POINT VALUE 75/60 on the F5J, which our F5J records as
epv 75 / bpv 60 — so the SSD prints EPV first and the D6J's 123/98 is epv 123, bpv 98.
The penal differences (owner, 2026-10-11: 'the main difference are the Center Warp boxes
- centerWarp, which no standard D6 has. The boom carries WRP-C, IMP, WRP-C: two centre
warp boxes and the emergency impulse. Annex: 'The F5J penal ship has a different boom
from other F5s.' Neither can move the ship unless the boom separates (G12.102).
- security doubled, 2 to 4, for the prisoners.
Everything else — shields, hull, power, control, tables, auxiliaries, weapons — is the D6's.
Shield 4 cross-checks: nine B-refit boxes are drawn beside it, and 13 + 9 = 22, the value
the B refit gives every shield.
_refitComment: The sheet states both costs: B REFIT (Y165) = +4, Y175 REFIT = +2, and in as many words that
'THE UIM REFIT IS NOT AVAILABLE FOR THIS SHIP' — so unlike the D6 there is no u refit here,
and no K phaser refit is offered either.
The rack note on the sheet: the ship began with type-F racks (one reload); the B refit converts
them to type-A (FD3.1) with one reload, lifting the FD3.6 restrictions and the chance of chain
reactions; the Y175 refit takes them to type-B (FD3.2) with two reloads.
The B refit does NOT lengthen the disruptors. The D6's does — 22 to 30 — and copying that
across because the D6J is a D6 hull would have been wrong; the penal ship keeps range 22 for
good (owner, 2026-10-11). The refit here converts the racks and adds the shield boxes, and
